title: Fletcher Henderson, Noble Sissle, Eubie Blake and the song 'One Day'
summary: Brief remarks on Henderson, Sissle and Blake, then Rasch asks what show 'One Day' was for and says goodnight.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Uh-huh. You know, you worked with Fletcher Henderson on the Jazz Train, and I guess in other shows too. What was he like?
Very fine guy. Very fine fellow. Gentleman in everything and terrific musician.

Uh-huh. And there were people that, you wonder what they were like, like I see names here, you know, I picked a few, like Noble Sissle. Can you just -- do you have any memories or any anecdotes or any stories about any of the --
That's true. That's very true. All right, what about Eubie Blake? You got any anecdotes or any little -- you know, reminiscences?
He thinks the same of you. You know, your song, One Day?
What show did you write that for?
I don't remember it, what show right at this moment.
Uh-huh. I'll have to wait -- I'll have to wait for you to come back home. Uh-huh.
Right. Now, maybe I'll give you a call a little later, let you rest a bit, then call you back. How's that?
All right. Kind of running out of air.
Yeah, I don't want you to do that. I sort of sense that. All right. Again, love and kisses from everybody up here. Okay, bye-bye.
